text.p: Shares of Slovenian brokerage Dadas surged 12.32 percent on Tuesday, but traders said the poor trading volume of only 30 shares had diminished the significance of the strong gain.

"I cannot see any logical reason for such an increase, and apart from that volume was very low. Dadas is one of those shares whose future moves are very difficult to predict," said Primoz Merhar, a trader at brokerage Proxy.
Dadas jumped 12.32 percent or 850 tolars to close at 7,750 tolars on volume of 30 shares for total turnover of 231,700 tolars.

Trading volumes in Dadas have been very small since March of last year, when the Securities' Market Agency started procedurees to ban Dadas' brokerage arm from trading, claiming it was rigging prices among its affiliated companies.
Since then, the share has fallen some 97 percent, while volume is down to a fraction of its previous daily average of more than 1,000 shares per day.
